stem: An adult client is prescribed the standard 3-day oral aprepitant regimen for chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting prevention together with oral dexamethasone. Which dexamethasone adjustment is expected because of the aprepitant interaction?

options.A: Reduce the oral dexamethasone dose by approximately 50%
options.B: Increase the oral dexamethasone dose by approximately 50%
options.C: Make no dexamethasone adjustment because aprepitant does not affect its exposure
options.D: Discontinue dexamethasone solely because it is contraindicated with aprepitant

rationale: Current aprepitant labeling states that the 3-day aprepitant regimen increases dexamethasone exposure and recommends reducing the oral dexamethasone dose by approximately 50%. The label does not recommend increasing the dose, leaving it unchanged in this regimen, or treating dexamethasone as contraindicated. Therefore A is the best answer.
educational_objective: Recognize the clinically significant aprepitant-dexamethasone interaction and the labeled recommendation to reduce oral dexamethasone by approximately 50% during the standard 3-day aprepitant regimen.
source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine — DailyMed
source_locator: §2.1 Prevention of Chemotherapy Induced Nausea and Vomiting, dosing tables/footnotes: 50% dexamethasone dosage reduction recommended to account for interaction with aprepitant; §7.1 Table 10, Dexamethasone: increased dexamethasone exposure; 3-day aprepitant regimen — reduce oral dexamethasone by approximately 50%
source_claim_supported: During the standard 3-day aprepitant regimen, aprepitant increases dexamethasone exposure and the label recommends an approximately 50% reduction in oral dexamethasone dose.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12 / PDF p.16: identify medication interactions, indications, and monitor/evaluate medication therapy
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — drug interaction / aprepitant and dexamethasone
correction_summary: Replaced the broad, weakly sourced statement that dexamethasone merely 'enhances the antiemetic effect' with a directly labeled, clinically actionable interaction. Added the exact approximately-50% oral dexamethasone dose reduction only in the specified 3-day aprepitant regimen, where the current label directly supports that precision.
audit_findings: A reproduces the current label intervention for the specified regimen. B reverses the required adjustment, C contradicts the documented exposure increase, and D falsely treats dexamethasone as contraindicated. The stem explicitly limits the scenario to the standard 3-day oral aprepitant regimen and oral dexamethasone, avoiding confusion with a single 40-mg aprepitant dose, for which the label states no oral dexamethasone adjustment is needed. One best answer remains; the numerical adjustment is directly source-supported. NCSBN 2026 mapping is direct.

final_reaudit_scope: current official DailyMed interaction/dosing; exact locator; claim-by-claim; A-D distractor audit; ambiguity/second-answer/cueing; NCSBN 2026 blueprint; independent adversarial second pass
